newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on exports, crush pace.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on exports, crush pace.

text.p: Bullish input from the export and crush sectors boosted CBOT soybean futures to a higher close, traders said.
"The fundamentals supported us, it was up on the sales numbers this morning," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soybeans for the week ended December 12 totaled 707,800 tonnes, above expectations for 500,000 to 600,000 tonnes.
The Census Bureau's November crush report released Thursday also spawned support in soybean futures, traders said.
The Census said the U.S. soybean crush pace during November was 133 million bushels, above the 127 million crushed in October and well above the 123.3 million crushed during November, 1995.
But gains were limited by near-perfect crop weather in key South American soybean growing areas, the traders said.
In late dealings, A.G. Edwards bought one million bushels of January. "There is a little fund buying again," a trader said. "Rand and Refco bought the March (late)."
Soybeans closed one to five cents per bushel higher, with January up 3-3/4 cents at $7.07-3/4 a bushel.
ADM Investor Services bought 2.5 million bushels of March, Cargill Inc sold four million May and USA Trading sold two million bushels of January, traders said.
The Chicago Corp bull spread two million bushels of January/March and Central Soya did 1.5 million bushels of January/March, the traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 43,000 contracts, below the 65,933 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In soybean options, First American sold 400 January $6.50 puts and sold 600 January $6.75 puts, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, below the 19,648 contracts traded Wednesday.
